title: Windows: check the Mac session's mixed-language follow-up on the GPU and ship the next version
description: The Mac session merged a6f67b4 into shared Engine code (MIX_PAD_MS = 30 for Silero padding so short pauses split; mlx quick piece check). Rerun the Windows GPU check on mixed-language clips (invented or fixture audio only), then build, install and release the next Windows version (GitHub release with the .exe).
notes: GPU check on fixture audio (es_climb + breath + en_fox): pieces split, but turbo's quick check heard the Spanish piece as English at 0.87, so the English half was dropped. Fix: a quick answer under QUICK_SURE = 0.95 is checked the full way (all wrong quick answers in 967 fixture pieces were under 0.95). New GPU test test_mixed_dictation_after_a_breath. Version 1.11.1.
close_reason: Closed

title: 'Coach me' prompt for Claude
description: A button that builds a prompt from recent dictations to people (not to AI apps) and copies it, asking Claude for the user's 3 recurring patterns, before -> after rewrites of their own sentences, and one habit to try this week. Text leaves the computer only when the user pastes it.

title: Clarity score + words Whisper struggled with
description: Save Whisper's word/segment confidence (avg_logprob, word probabilities) with each dictation in the local history. Insights: clarity score per dictation and trend; list of words with low confidence (mumbled/unclear), per language (also a pronunciation check for Greek/Spanish). Fills from new dictations onward. Engine change on both platforms (faster-whisper word_timestamps / mlx).
notes: Built: Engine.word_confidence (second pass with word timestamps after the paste, ~0.26 s on turbo; only with Insights on and no dictation waiting; the pill isn't kept busy). History gets speech_s, clarity (% words at p>=0.8), heard, unsure (p<0.5). Insights card 'How clearly you speak': score, 8-week trend, words it wasn't sure of per language. Mac: dictado-9jc.6.

title: Speech coaching: help the user speak more clearly from how they dictate
description: The user wants to improve how they speak using their dictation history. Research basis: ASR confidence correlates with intelligibility; immediate feedback reduces filler words without raising anxiety; hedges and hesitations lower perceived confidence; comprehension peaks around 130-160 wpm. Caveat: most dictation is thinking aloud to an AI, so coaching focuses on dictations to people (messages, email) and later the user's side of meetings. Everything computed locally; nothing personal ever goes in git (tests use invented text).

title: Repo clarity: one README for Windows + Mac, docs per OS, packaging/windows, a .dmg on releases
description: The repo didn't make clear it is one app for Windows and macOS, and releases only carried the Windows .exe. README for both (downloads table, requirements and install per OS, how the code is organised), docs/windows.md + docs/mac.md, packaging/windows/ next to packaging/macos/, and the Mac session attaches the .dmg to each release.
close_reason: PR #33 (README for both, docs/windows.md + docs/mac.md, packaging/windows); the Mac session attached the .dmg to v1.10.0 and corrected docs/mac.md (#36).

title: Dictation in mixed languages: detect per piece when the language is unclear
description: A dictation that switches language (e.g. Spanish then Greek) came out in one language: dictation picked one language per recording, so the other part was translated or dropped. Engine._run: cut at short pauses, detect each piece among the configured languages, transcribe each run in its own language; one run = one pass as before.
notes: Mac part done in #34 (mlx quick piece check + MIX_PAD_MS = 30). Windows GPU check (dictado-l2x) found turbo's quick check unreliable on short pieces; fixed with QUICK_SURE.
close_reason: PR #29, installed in 1.10.0 on Windows and released; Mac check pending in FEATURES.md.

title: Dictation with no text box under the cursor: keep it on the clipboard and say so
description: When the cursor isn't in a text box at the stop (the user clicked away), the dictation went nowhere. At the paste, UI Automation's focused element decides: clearly no text box -> no Ctrl+V (it would fire a shortcut there), the text stays on the clipboard, the pill says so, Home's Last dictation says Not pasted. Unknown -> paste as before. Mac: dictado-cd2.
close_reason: PR #27, installed in 1.9.0 on Windows.

title: Live text on the pill while dictating + catch dictations that come back much too short
description: Show the transcript live on the pill while dictating, and catch dictations that come back far shorter than the talking (seen on long dictations; not reproduced on test audio). Live: quick greedy pass every 2 s on the last 15 s, skipped whenever the model is busy/loading; the careful pass is still what gets pasted. Diagnostics: delivered log gets speech_s + dropout_s; a result under 4 chars/s on >= 15 s keeps its audio locally in data/suspect (last 5).
notes: Reopened 2026-10-07 for the Mac session's findings: previews ran with no pill to show them (Ui always has live), and a stop tap could wait up to one preview pass.
close_reason: Merged #22 (live text) and #26 (only when the pill can show it; slow passes stretch the gap).

title: Rename Dictado -> Ecoscribe
description: Rename before going public: 'Dictado' clashes with Dictato (a paid local Mac dictation app) and several iPhone apps.
design: Phase 1 (this): everything visible -> Ogma: window/tray/pill/toasts/prompts, installer display names + Setup file names, README/FEATURES/guide, GitHub repo ErikBros/ogma (redirect). Internals unchanged: package dictado, Dictado.exe, data dirs, Run key, bundle id, MCP key. Phase 2 (after the Mac stack merges): package rename, exe name, data dir migration, installer upgrade from Dictado (old dir + Run key), MCP key, Mac bundle id (re-grant TCC), speaker add-on name.
notes: Ogma was dropped; Echotype/Echoscribe are taken in transcription; picked Ecoscribe (6 repos, none voice; GitHub user free). Phase 2 Windows half: PR #17 (package ecoscribe, Ecoscribe.exe 1.7.0, paths.migrate for Win + Mac dirs, installer upgrade from Dictado, Run key + Claude link renamed). Mac half: PR #20. Windows speaker add-on name: dictado-jtv.
close_reason: Both halves merged and installed: Windows (PR #17, 1.7.0, data/Run key/Claude link moved) and Mac (PR #20, Ecoscribe.app, TCC re-granted). Windows speaker add-on name: dictado-jtv.

comments.author: ErikBros
comments.text:
Mac session: rename phase 2 (Windows half) is merged in main (b6a89d2), so you can start your half (ticket dictado-c9u): Ecoscribe.app, bundle ids, speakers app, LaunchAgent, TCC, darwin migrate test.

What is already in main:
- the package is `ecoscribe`; env vars are ECOSCRIBE_* (ECOSCRIBE_DATA_DIR), except DICTADO_SPEAKERS_* / DICTADO_VERSION in the Mac/speakers build scripts
- `paths.MAC_DIR` = ~/Library/Application Support/Ecoscribe; `paths.migrate_all()` runs first thing in main() and moves ~/Library/Application Support/Dictado there (skipped when ECOSCRIBE_DATA_DIR is set, and while the old app holds Dictado/run/DictadoSingleInstance.lock). Please add the darwin test (tests/test_paths_migrate.py has the shared ones; the Windows-pairs test is skipped on darwin)
- lock/socket names are Local\\Ecoscribe* (ipc, commands, sysutil); log/pid are ecoscribe.log / ecoscribe.pid
- Left untouched for you: Dictado.app, com.erikbros.dictado (bundle id + LaunchAgent label), packaging/macos/dictado-mac.spec, tools/build_mac.py names, dictado-systap, "Dictado Speakers.app", systap.swift strings
- Claude app link: mcpServers.dictado is renamed to ecoscribe at start (frozen builds); is_connected accepts both
- Version is 1.7.0. The Windows speaker add-on name is ticket dictado-jtv.

title: Languages as add-ons: base English + Swedish, 'Add a language' for the rest
description: Languages as add-ons: English and Swedish built in, everything else added from an 'Add a language' picker in Settings (no download; Whisper knows ~99).
design: Base: en, sv. [whisper] extra_languages = added codes. Everywhere (dictation checkboxes, meeting/file language lists, tray, prompt) offers base + added; meetings also get 'Mixed: your languages' (detected per piece) + Detect. Dictation model: large-v3 when any chosen language isn't one turbo handles well (sv, el and lower-resource ones). Names for any code via a shared table checked against faster-whisper's list. Removing an added language also drops it from the dictation set.
close_reason: Merged to main and shipped in Ecoscribe 1.6.0 (installed on Windows 2026-10-07).

title: Dictation: your languages (any mix of en/es/sv/el), auto-detect among them, language shown on the pill, Right Ctrl+L forces the next one
description: Choose which languages dictation listens for (any mix), auto-detected among them; the pill shows the language it heard; dictation key + L forces the next one.
design: Settings: multi-select languages (en, es, sv, el; any mix, Greek new for dictation), saved without a restart where possible. Auto: detect among only those per dictation; sticky toward the last language when the call is close. Model: sv or el in the set -> large-v3 (int8_float16), else turbo. Pill: '✓ ES' briefly after the paste when >1 language. Override: hold the dictation key + L cycles the NEXT dictation Auto -> EN -> ES -> SV -> EL -> Auto, pill shows it; L swallowed. Windows in this PR; Mac key = new capability row with a macos ticket.
close_reason: Merged to main and shipped in Ecoscribe 1.6.0 (installed on Windows 2026-10-07).

title: Real call detection check on macOS
description: Actual Teams/Slack/Zoom/Meet/FaceTime/Signal calls raise the prompt and stop after the call. Needs Erik on a call. Was uat.9/13.

description: Swift helper, macOS 14.4+: record the computer's audio next to the mic; Me/Others labels, live transcript, recovery after a crash mid-call. Was uat.8.

title: Mac: word confidence from mlx for the Insights clarity score
description: dictado-9jc.1 saves how sure Whisper was of each word (a second pass with word timestamps after the paste, Engine.word_confidence). The mlx model ignores word_timestamps, so on the Mac no clarity is saved and Insights says so. Make MlxWhisperModel.transcribe return segments with .words (word, probability) when word_timestamps=True (mlx_whisper.transcribe supports word_timestamps), then check the Insights clarity card fills on the Mac.

title: GitHub Support: purge old commits after the history reset
description: The public history was reset to one root commit to remove personal data from old commit messages and ticket versions. Old commits stay reachable through refs/pull/* and cached views until GitHub Support purges them. Owner action: send the prepared request at support.github.com (Remove sensitive data). Close when GitHub confirms.

title: Fillers and hedges: optional immediate feedback + weekly trend
description: Opt-in: after a dictation to people, the pill notes filler words/hedges ('like x4'); weekly trend in Insights. Hedges list (kind of, maybe, I don't know, I think, sort of) per language. Neutral wording (fillers are discourse markers, not errors).

title: Insights tab: what your words say (opt-in in Settings)
description: An opt-in Insights tab (Settings switch) with what the dictation history says: time saved against typing, words per minute, streak, when (hour of day, last 14 days) and where (apps) you dictate, languages, speaking habits (filler words per 100 words, shown neutrally; repeated phrases), names Whisper keeps misspelling with one-click 'Add to Your words', and 'Your week for Claude' (copies the week's dictations as a prompt). Computed locally; nothing leaves the computer. Personal data never goes in the repo: tests and demo use invented text, tests/test_no_personal_data.py guards it.
close_reason: PR #37, installed and released as 1.11.0 on Windows; personal-data guard tests/test_no_personal_data.py; repo history reset to one clean commit.

Mac: AXFocusedUIElement's role (AXTextField/AXTextArea/AXComboBox editable = text; AXList/AXButton/AXOutline/Finder icon view = other; anything else unknown -> paste) in platform/macos/deliver.py.

title: Numpad Enter as a second dictation key (Windows)
description: Let the numpad's Enter (bottom-right corner of the keyboard, easy to reach) start and stop dictation like the dictation key. Settings > Numpad Enter dictates too: the numpad's Enter (VK_RETURN + LLKHF_EXTENDED) acts as the dictation key in the hook (tap, hold, Esc cancel) and is swallowed; the main Enter is untouched. Off by default. Mac: dictado-1k7.
close_reason: PR #25, installed in 1.9.0 on Windows (Settings > Numpad Enter dictates too, off by default).

title: macOS: live text on the pill while dictating
description: Windows has it (dictado-v67): App calls ui.live(text) every ~2 s while recording; the Mac Overlay (platform/macos/shell.py) needs a live(text) that widens the panel to two lines of text under the timer, like platform/windows/shell.py _dictating_pill. Engine.preview is shared (mlx path: check beam_size=1 is honoured and the pass stays under ~1 s for 15 s).
close_reason: PR #30 (Mac session): Overlay.live on the Mac pill; real desktop: live text at 8 s of a 10.6 s dictation, 100 % recall, 772 ms stop-to-paste.

title: macOS: dictation key + L picks the next dictation's language
description: Windows (dictado-bvf): holding the dictation key and pressing L emits a 'lang' action (App.cycle_language: Auto -> each configured language -> Auto), the L is swallowed, auto-repeat cycles once. Mac keyhook needs the same: with Right Command held, L (keycode 37) -> emit ('lang', ...), swallow down+up. The rest (App, engine, pill flash, tray 'Next dictation in', Settings checkboxes) is shared.
close_reason: PR #11, real desktop run.

title: install_check counts the app's own hook and watchdog processes as extra instances
description: tests/e2e/install_check.py checks 'exactly one Ecoscribe.exe running' and 'two processes: engine + window' by counting every Ecoscribe.exe. The app now starts its own children (--hook, the low-level keyboard hook process, and --supervise, the watchdog), so the checks fail on a healthy install (1.11.1: 42/46, all four failures are these counts). Count main instances only (command line without --hook / --supervise / --engine-worker).

title: Meetings: the user's talk share, monologues, questions, hedges
description: From real meeting transcripts (Me / Others): talk-to-listen ratio, monologues over 90 s, questions asked, hedges on the user's side. Needs real meetings recorded first.

title: Pace per dictation and pause share
description: Words per minute per dictation and the share of pauses (audio vs speech after VAD), with the 130-160 wpm comprehension range as information, not a goal. Split: to people vs to AI apps.

title: GPU test: dictation latency during a job fails while the installed Ecoscribe holds the GPU
description: test_meeting_gpu::test_dictation_latency_unchanged_during_a_job fails on main too (2026-10-07: busy-base ~750 ms > 200 ms) while the installed app's engine worker and desktop apps use 4.7 of 8 GB. Make it measure with the app's worker stopped (or skip with a reason when another process holds > N GB), so the GPU suite is green on Erik's PC.

title: macOS: the numpad's Enter as a second dictation key
description: Windows has [hotkey] numpad_enter (HookThread.numpad_alias): the numpad's Enter acts as the dictation key and is swallowed. On the Mac, keyboards with a numpad send keycode 76 (Enter); the keyhook would map it the same way and swallow it. Erik uses Windows; the Mac Settings row is hidden until this lands.
close_reason: PR #35 (Mac session).

title: Windows speaker add-on: DictadoSpeakers.exe / Dictado-Speakers-Setup -> Ecoscribe names
description: Rename phase 2 (dictado-c9u) left the Windows speaker add-on as is: Programs\Dictado Speakers\DictadoSpeakers.exe, Dictado-Speakers-Setup-<ver>.exe, built in %USERPROFILE%\dictado-build. Renaming needs a new add-on build (4.6 GB) and the app looking in both places, so an installed 1.1.0 add-on keeps working.
close_reason: PR #24: EcoscribeSpeakers.exe / Ecoscribe-Speakers-Setup 1.2.0, built and installed on Windows (old Dictado Speakers removed), 12 turns on CUDA from the installed exe.
